title: Localization residues of unit Kummer symbols when divisor purity is given
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $A=\mathbf F_\ell$, and let $Y$ be a regular Noetherian scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Let $f\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ be a nonzerodivisor, let $i:D=V(f)\hookrightarrow Y$ be its regular effective Cartier divisor, and put $j:U=Y-D\hookrightarrow Y$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. Assume, as a hypothesis, that the supported Kummer fundamental class $A_D\to i^!A_Y(1)[2]$ of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] is an isomorphism. Use ordinary small-etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], twists, including negative twists defined by the dual Tate line [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist, lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], and ordinary cup products [def-wf-ordinary-etale-cup]. There are localization exact sequences, for every integer $t$,
$$\cdots\longrightarrow H^{q-2}(D,A(t-1))\longrightarrow H^q(Y,A(t))\xrightarrow{j^*}H^q(U,A(t))\xrightarrow{\operatorname{res}_f}H^{q-1}(D,A(t-1))\longrightarrow H^{q+1}(Y,A(t))\longrightarrow\cdots.$$
Groups in negative degree are zero. Normalize the residue by a single overall sign so that $\operatorname{res}_f(\kappa(f))=1$, where $\kappa$ is the Kummer connecting homomorphism [lem-amb-kummer-any-base]. For units $g_1,\ldots,g_b$ on $Y$, put $\alpha=\kappa(g_1)\cup\cdots\cup\kappa(g_b)\in H^b(Y,A(b))$, with $\alpha=1$ when $b=0$. Then
$$\operatorname{res}_f(j^*\alpha)=0,\qquad \operatorname{res}_f\bigl(\kappa(f)\cup j^*\alpha\bigr)=i^*\alpha\in H^b(D,A(b)).$$
The localization sequences are natural in the coefficient sheaf: for an integer $c$ and a global section $\beta\in H^0(Y,A(c))$, cup product with $j^*\beta$, $\beta$ and $i^*\beta$ maps the sequence for $t$ to the sequence for $t+c$, so that $\operatorname{res}_f(x\cup j^*\beta)=\operatorname{res}_f(x)\cup i^*\beta$ for every $x\in H^q(U,A(t))$. These formulas are valid without excellence; they assume purity of this divisor and do not assert it. They use the same restriction maps on unit Kummer classes as the Kummer sequence.
